questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Most crucial was the language: I was motivated to improve my proficiency in the language of the host university. The culture of the country also attracted me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a great time but was perhaps a little overly ambitious in only choosing courses in the local language.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There were introductory events set up to disseminate the information, but it was quite difficult to get in touch with the coordinators for international students and to know which offices to report to.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Guidance over e-mail, introductory events, limited cousel from the department for international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The direction des affaires internationales was really difficult to get a hold of, though friendly and helpful when I did get through to them. They seemed understaffed to me.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: not exceedingly difficult. I found mine through the group "Deutsche in Paris". Can highly recommend using these national networks.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's great! Living on campus wasn't an option at Assas. Although living in la cité internationale was an option, that's about the closest you could've gotten to living on campus. This seemed very nice as well, and they had some great events going.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were multiple steps required and it didn't always seem apparent what I had to do and when. A new online system had just been introduced through which to choose subjects which worked very poorly.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First there was inscription administrative, for which I waited in line for a long time in front of an office before being told that the office for inscription administrative didn't do international students. I was then sent to the direction des affaires internationales, which was exceptionally closed twice both times I came despite the office door saying it would be open on the previous day. I had hustled over from a different campus because the only opening time which suited the intro week schedule for international students left little time to make it over, so a sweaty and desperate appearance got me in the second time, where I was quickly helped. Then came the inscription pédagogique, which consisted of the choice of subjects. Was supposed to work online; didnt; I got it fixed at the direction des affaires internationales.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The local students were most helpful! The administration was quite helpful when I succeeded in getting through to them. There was helpful information from the administration in the intro week.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very! I enrolled in all the courses that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience, don't stress too much, and know that you can argue your case with the administration. Rules aren't necessarily hard rules as such: you can oftentimes talk or charm your way around them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very different to the University of Copenhagen (my host university). The lectures generally weren't accompanied by slides, and the use of textbooks was rare. It was very much a sit-and-listen-and-take-notes type of deal.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: One of my courses was Ba, the other four were Masters. Us international students had fewer courses than the local students, which was offset by the fact that the courses were rendered somewhat more difficult by being in French.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. Less interactive, more of a reading with many of the professors. There were usually no accompanying visual aids (e.g. PP slides) or textbook readings.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Droit pénal international et européen
Grand systèmes de droit contemporains
Histoire du droit international
Histoire comparée des institutions des pays de l'Europe
Philosophie du droit

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Grand systèmes de droit contemporains, Histoire du droit international, Histoire comparée des institutions des pays de l'Europe, Philosophie du droit. That is to say, all of them except Droit pénal international et européen. The professor, Monsieur Didier Rebut, is difficult to understand and keeps on talking even when the mic cuts off. The lectures are held in a very large lecture hall where the sound is less than optimal. The local students agreed that he's difficult to understand.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is a bit cheaper than Copenhagen. I can recommend applying for CAF (a bit like boligstøtte)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The sport I wanted which fit into my time schedule got cancelled because the gym it was supposed to be held in was under reconstruction, which wasn't properly communicated. I ended up not doing sports. There's a a ton of opportunities to join clubs though, which I can highly recommend I had a great time with the La From' Touch, Assas Environnement and Assas de Concert

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A whole lot which was available through the clubs at the university

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Erasmus Student Network provides a lot of activities and trips to international students. I didn't participate myself but heard great things!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rue du Montparnasse

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it relatively easy! The locals made it quite easy I found.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: clubs! And they're nice, just talk to them!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the whole no toilet seats situation took a bit of getting used to

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The value placed in food

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: join a club, befriend locals from your courses to get good notes, check out the cultural activities at la cité internationale. Also the restaurant le quartier rouge is great, they have jazz jam sessions every Sunday.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The vélib bikes are a pretty great way to get around. Also get the navigo liberté card for public transport which just charges your transits to your card at the end of the month.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and speaking lots of french!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The struggle with the administration

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy the city!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
